findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() - unwrap on file I/O panics on missing or unreadable files
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err to convert io::Error into a typed variant

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() - unwrap on numeric parse panics on non-numeric input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV values abort the program instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use map_err to convert ParseIntError into a typed ParseError::Invalid variant

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string performs file I/O directly inside a function that should be separated into shell/domain layers
findings.failure_mode: I/O coupling prevents pure testing of parsing logic and violates Functional Core / Imperative Shell
findings.fix: extract I/O into a shell function that reads bytes and passes them to a pure parse_sensors(lines: &[str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) - stdout logging hidden in parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: side effect in core logic prevents deterministic testing and leaks shell concern into domain
findings.fix: remove println! from parsing; logging belongs in the shell layer after domain construction

findings.problem: parts[0] - unchecked indexing on Vec<usize> with no bounds validation
findings.failure_mode: empty or single-field lines panic via index out of bounds
findings.fix: validate parts.len() >= 2 before indexing, or use parts.get(0).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? and parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?

findings.problem: parts[1] - unchecked indexing on Vec<usize> with no bounds validation
findings.failure_mode: lines with only one field panic via index out of bounds

findings.problem: as u16 cast from u32 parse result - lossy conversion silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: sensor values in range 65536-4294967295 silently wrap to incorrect u16 values, producing wrong data
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) or parse directly as u16: line.split_once(',').ok_or(...).and_then(|(_, v)| v.trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(...))

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() - collects into unbounded Vec without capacity limits
findings.failure_mode: adversarial input with thousands of comma-separated fields triggers unbounded heap allocation
findings.fix: limit field count with a domain cap before collecting; use try_reserve on the Vec or limit to expected field count with take(max_fields)

findings.problem: Record.name uses raw String instead of a domain newtype
findings.failure_mode: no compile-time guarantee that name is non-empty or valid; illegal sensor names are representable
findings.fix: define struct SensorName(String) with a smart constructor validating non-empty, then use SensorName in Record

findings.problem: load_sensors returns Vec<Record> with no Result wrapper - all errors are swallowed by unwrap
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish between I/O failures, parse errors, overflow, or invalid data
findings.fix: define enum LoadError { Io(io::Error), Invalid, Overflow, Allocation } and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: No try_reserve or domain cap on Vec allocation before collecting parsed fields
findings.failure_mode: unbounded allocation on hostile input; allocation failure returns OOM instead of typed error
findings.fix: validate line count against a domain cap, then call values.try_reserve(line_count).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? before the collect

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence for load_sensors performance characteristics
findings.failure_mode: performance claims about CSV loading are unmeasured; allocation behavior on large files is unknown
findings.fix: add a criterion or custom benchmark measuring throughput, allocations, and memory for realistic file sizes

findings.problem: No fmt, check, clippy, or test evidence present in task crate
findings.failure_mode: style violations, dead code, and lint issues are undetected
findings.fix: run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy with strict gates, and cargo test

findings.problem: File I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing (split/parse), domain construction (Record), and side effects (println) are all fused in one function
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test parsing logic in isolation; no pure domain layer exists
findings.fix: split into shell_fn read_sensor_file(path) -> Result<String, LoadError> and pure domain_fn parse_sensor_lines(&str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>
